svg.title: Multi-environment AWS architecture
svg.desc: GitHub Actions deploys a static site to separate staging and production CloudFront and private S3 origins using OIDC roles. Terraform provisions each environment's VPC, load balancer, private EC2 Auto Scaling group, and static hosting. Each environment has a separate Terraform state key in a shared state bucket.
svg.text: Terraform provisions isolated staging and production stacks; GitHub Actions publishes the static site through short-lived AWS credentials.
Syncs site files and invalidates CDN
One account by default · staging/prod can use separate AWS accounts for stronger isolation
Actions syncs HTML/CSS to S3 and invalidates CloudFront
Private subnets · across two Availability Zones
Security groups allow app traffic from ALB only; no inbound SSH
Actions syncs HTML/CSS to S3 and invalidates CloudFront
Private subnets · across two Availability Zones
NAT gateway per AZ · Session Manager access
Security groups allow app traffic from ALB only; no inbound SSH
Separate Terraform roots and state keys
Use separate accounts for stronger boundaries.
Infrastructure and static hosting are separate paths: the sample HTML site does not call the EC2 service. Terraform apply is manual; the Actions workflow deploys site files only.
